questions.question: What are custom hooks and how do you write a good one?
questions.title: Custom Hooks
questions.direct_answer: A custom hook is a function whose name starts with `use` that calls other hooks — the mechanism for extracting and reusing stateful logic across components. It's not a component, has no markup, and each component calling it gets its OWN state instances (no sharing). Good ones: single responsibility, stable return shape (tuple or object), accept config, clean up their effects, and handle all edge cases (loading, error, unmount races) so callers don't repeat that logic.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CH[custom hook: use...-function] -->|calls| H[useState / useEffect / others]
    C1[Component A] -->|inlines slots| CH
    C2[Component B] -->|inlines slots| CH
    C1 -.independent state.-> S1[A's slots]
    C2 -.independent state.-> S2[B's slots]
    E[return shape = the API] --> T[tuple for pairs / object for named]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
Why the mechanism works (the internals): hooks don't live IN components — they live in React's per-instance hook slots, keyed by call order. A custom hook is INLINED into the calling component's slot sequence: useDebouncedValue contributes its useState slot and useEffect slot to the CALLER's list. That's why rules-of-hooks apply across the custom-hook boundary (a conditional custom hook call breaks the caller's slot order) and why two components calling the same custom hook get separate state (different component instances = different slot lists).

The design patterns (the reusable catalog):
- Adapter hooks: wrap a browser/3rd-party API in React semantics (useLocalStorage — state that syncs to storage; useMediaQuery — reactive viewport state)
- Data hooks: useFetch(url) encapsulating loading/error/abort — though production teams usually adopt React Query/SWR for this entire class (caching, dedupe, retries beat hand-rolled)
- Behaviour hooks: useDebouncedValue, useThrottle, usePrevious, useIntersectionObserver (lazy-load images), useClickOutside (dropdowns/modals)
- State machine hooks: useReducer wrappers formalizing domain flows (useCart, useCheckout)

The testing story (the follow-up): custom hooks are testable via renderHook (React Testing Library) — render the hook in a test harness, act() on the returns, assert state transitions, and test the timer/subscription cleanup by unmounting and asserting no post-unmount updates. This is the specific advantage over extracting logic into a plain function: plain functions can't hold state; custom hooks are stateful units with a test seam.
